page: Amazon Web Services mac1.metal is a bare-metal instance configuration providing access to macOS environments running on dedicated Intel hardware. The machine is driven by a 6-core Intel x86_64 processor operating at a base frequency of 3.2 GHz. With hyper-threading configured at two threads per physical core, the instance provides 12 dedicated vCPUs. System memory is provisioned at 32.0 GB of RAM, resulting in an allocation of 2.67 GB per virtual processing core. The system contains no discrete GPU accelerators.

Storage and networking configurations reflect a networked architecture. The mac1.metal instance includes no local storage disks, requiring persistent data and operating volumes to be attached across the network. Networking performance is specified with a baseline throughput of 25 Gbps. The instance comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating standard virtual private cloud network routing for inbound and outbound communication.

Designed primarily for continuous integration and delivery pipelines, mac1.metal serves workloads requiring native x86 macOS environments. Key use cases encompass compiling, packaging, and testing applications for iOS, macOS, watchOS, and tvOS. The absence of onboard NVMe storage represents an operational tradeoff, requiring external network bandwidth to support application asset transfer and operating disk activity.
description: Amazon Web Services mac1.metal provides dedicated bare-metal macOS execution powered by an Intel 6-core processor operating at 3.2 GHz. Built on the x86_64_mac architecture, it delivers 12 vCPUs via two threads per core alongside 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.67 GB of RAM per vCPU. The server incorporates no integrated local storage disks, requiring external network-attached volumes for all data persistence. Network connectivity is supported by a 25 Gbps baseline bandwidth. Lacking discrete GPUs, mac1.metal serves as a dedicated platform tailored for Apple ecosystem software build farms, automated testing, continuous integration pipelines, and compilation tasks requiring native Intel macOS compatibility.
